source_bindings.role: alloc/dealloc/realloc counter updates and live/peak accounting
System allocator wrapper records only successful old/new request sizes
synthetic XML/archive generator, source opening, and ownership-mode regions
full XML/inventory parse, changed target construction, and full-buffer replacement
Arc-backed inventory clone and retained-byte estimate
catalog-only open and deferred main XML materialization/query

counter_semantics.allocated_bytes: sum of successful alloc/alloc_zeroed request sizes plus new_size for every successful realloc
counter_semantics.deallocated_bytes: sum of successful dealloc request sizes plus old_size for every successful realloc
counter_semantics.allocation_calls: fresh allocation calls plus successful realloc calls
counter_semantics.live_bytes: allocated_bytes minus deallocated_bytes at the callback boundary
not_measured: whether realloc moved or extended in place
physical writes, unique object ownership, or RSS

source_corpus.derivation: count UTF-8 bytes of the exact source_document strings, including retention-section-{index:03} expansion; reported archive sizes are compressed OPC bytes

topology_decomposition.method: c1 exact region = F + C; shared c8 = F + 8C; independent c8 = 8F + 8C; Snapshot/Inventory clones are Arc-backed shallow clones
topology_decomposition.interpretation: F is the one-time open/query path and C is topology-specific commit construction; neither term is parser-only or copy-only. Exact linearity is measured in the retained reports.

bounded_conclusions: Large construction-region requested traffic can include substantial realloc capacity churn because each realloc contributes its entire new_size to allocated_bytes.
The reports cannot determine how many reallocations moved or how many bytes were copied; no copy-volume or parser-only claim is made.

The independent/shared gap is source-topology evidence: independent mode repeats open/query for each source, while shared mode opens/query once and shallow-clones the snapshot. It does not isolate XML parsing from package indexing or inventory allocation.

after_snapshot_drop is the construction/query/commit boundary. Correctness publication and inverse validation occur afterward, so commits_retained cumulative allocated_bytes must not be relabeled construction traffic.
future_evidence_required: Record phase-tagged successful allocator events with operation, pointer, old_size, new_size, returned pointer, alignment, and failure status.
Report fresh allocation request sum separately from realloc new_size sum; also report positive growth deltas, shrink deltas, moved-realloc count, and moved-byte semantic bounds.
Attribute events to open/query, edit/commit, XML replacement, and inventory parsing (or add source-level capacity telemetry for the major buffers) before inferring copied-byte or parser-cost shares.
Keep publication/validation in a separate phase so its allocations cannot enter a construction attribution.
limitations: This is a read-only post hoc audit of the retained 0931 packet; no build, workload, or capture was run.
The synthetic XML is highly compressible and is not representative corpus coverage.
The allocator callback is process-global and excludes allocator-internal overlap and RSS.
